articles.title: Comprehensive Imaging Review of the Ureter.
articles.abstract: The ureter is an important conduit between the kidney and the bladder and is frequently imaged to rule out cancer in the upper genitourinary tract. However, while malignancy can occur, a spectrum of other pathologic ureteral findings can exist, and these can be divided into congenital, intrinsic, and extrinsic abnormalities that range from postoperative and neoplastic conditions to inflammatory disease. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the ureter, including the ureteral anatomy, ureteral imaging strategies, and various ureteral conditions and their associated imaging features. It is important to identify congenital genitourinary variants, as these are frequently linked to further imaging recommendations, such as nuclear medicine renography and fluoroscopic voiding cystourethrography. Intrinsic abnormalities can be iatrogenic, infectious, inflammatory, or neoplastic. Intrinsic ureteral strictures are most commonly iatrogenic, usually resulting from prior surgery or radiation therapy. Ureteral infections include tuberculosis, schistosomiasis, and Escherichia coli infection, which have varying imaging manifestations. Inflammatory conditions include ureteritis cystica and pseudodiverticulosis. Ureteral masses are rarely benign and are most commonly urothelial carcinomas. Processes in the abdomen and pelvis, including mass effect from pregnancy, ureteral compression from advanced pelvic floor prolapse, and rarely, ureteral obstruction from vaginal devices, also can affect the ureter. The ureter can be injured during pelvic surgery or trauma. It also may be involved by deep pelvic endometriosis, mass effect from extrinsic lesions, or reactive change from inflammatory processes. Radiologists need to have a clear understanding of the patient's history and the range of possible ureteral conditions to establish the optimal differential diagnosis.

articles.title: Updated Terminology for Multidisciplinary Management of Intrauterine Devices: A Proposed Lexicon.
articles.abstract: There are numerous terms used to describe variant locations of intrauterine devices (IUDs) in US reports, such as displaced, low lying, and malpositioned. These vague terms are frequently misinterpreted by providers and patients, which may lead to an incorrect inference of inadequate contraception. Current consensus guidelines from the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) indicate that the greatest risk of unintended pregnancy may be due to the unnecessary removal of a nonfundal IUD. Many providers now advocate leaving an IUD in place if it is located entirely above the internal os, as the device still provides effective contraception. The ACOG recommends counseling for patients, whether symptomatic or asymptomatic, before removal of the IUD. The authors outline a simple lexicon to describe the location of IUDs in US reports that includes terms understood by obstetrics and gynecology providers and that better align with current gynecologic literature. ©RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Optimizing Sonographic Analysis of Superficial Soft-Tissue Masses.
articles.abstract: US is a highly effective imaging modality for the evaluation of superficial soft-tissue masses. The authors provide a practical and evidence-based guide for sonographers and radiologists, particularly those specializing in abdominal and musculoskeletal imaging, on how to optimize sonographic imaging and analysis of such lesions. Presented are best practices in image acquisition, a review of advanced imaging techniques, and discussion of image interpretation strategies, with the goal of improving lesion characterization and guiding clinical management.

articles.title: Prostate cancer screening with MRI: insights from the ESUR Prostate MRI Working Group.
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based screening for prostate cancer (PCa) remains controversial due to uncertain long-term benefits, overdiagnosis, and overtreatment of indolent disease. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has transformed the diagnostic pathway of PCa and is increasingly explored as a screening tool. This special report from the ESUR Prostate MRI Working Group provides an overview of current evidence and insights into the potential role of MRI in PCa screening. MRI-based screening strategies appear to improve detection of clinically significant PCa while reducing unnecessary biopsies and diagnoses of non-significant disease, though long-term outcome data, including mortality impact and interval cancer rates, remain limited. Biparametric MRI is particularly suited for screening due to its shorter acquisition time, reduced operational complexity, and lower costs compared with multiparametric MRI. Two main implementation approaches have emerged: MRI-first pathways, which maximise detection but require substantial resources, and risk-stratified strategies, in which MRI is used after initial assessment (e.g. PSA), potentially offering greater feasibility and cost-effectiveness. Evidence from large trials supports integrating MRI into screening pathways, particularly as a reflex test after PSA screening, although uncertainties remain regarding optimal protocols, interpretation thresholds, follow-up strategies, and long-term outcomes. Key barriers include limited MRI capacity, economic considerations, and the need for standardisation and quality assurance. Advances in artificial intelligence may further enhance efficiency. Overall, MRI has the potential to improve the balance between benefits and harms in PCa screening, but further evidence is required to define its optimal implementation. KEY POINTS: Question Can prostate MRI be effectively integrated into population-based prostate cancer screening pathways? Findings MRI-based screening improves detection of csPCa while reducing unnecessary biopsies; biparametric MRI should be the protocol of choice to enhance feasibility, although optimal implementation and long-term outcomes remain uncertain. Clinical relevance MRI may overcome key limitations of PSA-based screening by enhancing the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer while reducing harms such as overdiagnosis and unnecessary biopsies.

articles.title: CD70-Targeted PET/CT in a Patient with von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome and Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
Multimodal Visual Question Answering System for Survival Prognosis in PSMA-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
articles.abstract: Large language models show great promise for clinical decision support but generally lack medical imaging integration. Therefore, vision-language models have been proposed, but there is little evidence on their performance, particularly compared with conventional machine learning. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy is a well-established treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but it is still not known which patients will be good long-term responders. Therefore, this study proposes a physician-inspired visual question answering (VQA) framework that emulates the structured integration of PSMA-directed imaging and clinical data used in routine clinical assessment for overall survival prognostication. Methods: As a proof of concept, we conducted a retrospective, multicenter study across 2 academic institutions that included 110 patients with mCRPC who were treated with either [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T or [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Our VQA approach incorporates a 3-dimensional image encoder, the domain-specific language model RadBERT, and a cross-modal transformer to process baseline and interim (after 2 cycles) PET and SPECT images, clinical data, and clinical query. The model was trained to predict 24-mo survival, and performance was compared with state-of-the-art approaches. External validation was performed with the [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 cohort. Results: The VQA model outperformed all state-of-the-art approaches while showing accuracy comparable to the query-free attention multimodal fusion model. Specifically, it achieved 81.8% accuracy (95% CI, 0.52-0.95) when integrating SPECT or PET images with prostate-specific antigen measurements. External validation of the VQA showed 71.9% accuracy (95% CI, 0.53-0.86) after few-shot fine-tuning, with further improvement over all state-of-the-art approaches in survival stratification. The VQA approach showed the closest calibration with the ground-truth survival distribution, with no significant differences observed (log-rank test, P = 0.76). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed the highest area under the curve (0.75) among the evaluated models. Together, these findings suggest that the VQA approach demonstrated adaptability across different PSMA ligands while maintaining slightly improved yet comparable overall survival prognostic performance. Conclusion: By adopting a physician-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning. The preliminary results indicate that VQA-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: [18F]F-AraG PET Imaging of Immunometabolic Activity in Individuals Without Malignancy.
articles.abstract: [18F]F-AraG is a clinical-stage PET tracer in immuno-oncology that accumulates in activated T cells and tissues with high mitochondrial biogenesis. Characterizing its distribution in individuals without malignancy is essential for interpreting immunometabolic states relevant to cancer biology. Methods: Twenty adults without active malignancy underwent a single [18F]F-AraG PET/CT scan, with tracer uptake assessed in relation to clinical history, medications, and demographic and physiologic factors. Results: Bilateral brown adipose tissue activation was identified in 3 participants receiving potentially brown adipose tissue-activating medications, in the absence of cold exposure or fasting. One showed elevated vertebral bone marrow uptake, previously linked to poor survival in immune checkpoint inhibitor-treated lung cancer. One of 2 participants with breast implants showed asymmetric periimplant uptake. Posterior pulmonary uptake occurred in a subset of participants, often with prior respiratory conditions and thoracic lymph node uptake. Conclusion: Whole-body [18F]F-AraG PET captures diverse immunometabolic activity in individuals without malignancy, reflecting systemic processes that may influence cancer and treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Ultra-Low-Dose Long-Axial-Field-of-View [18F]FDG PET with CT-Free Attenuation Correction for Staging Hodgkin Lymphoma in Pregnancy.
Test-Retest Repeatability of [18F]FDG Uptake by Solid Tumors on PET/MRI: A Prospective, Multicenter Study Using the QIBA Protocol.
articles.abstract: Prior oncologic PET/MRI repeatability studies have been limited by single-center designs, small cohorts, or select patient populations. Our primary aim was to estimate the test-retest repeatability of uptake metrics on [18F]FDG PET/MRI studies across a variety of cancer types. A secondary aim was to assess the impact of intersession μ-map variability on repeatability. Methods: In this prospective study involving 2 institutions with different PET/MRI scanners, subjects completing standard-of-care [18F]FDG PET/CT or MRI examinations were recruited to undergo 2 research [18F]FDG PET/MRIs (i.e., test and retest) within a 1-9 d period per Quantitative Imaging Biomarker Alliance specifications. Enrollment required at least 1 measurable lesion (long axis ≥ 2 cm, known or expected SUVmax ≥ 4.0) and no active oncologic therapy. SUVmax and SUVpeak were extracted from measurable lesions (1-5 per subject). At site 1, attenuation-coefficient maps (i.e., μ-maps) were inspected for substantial differences across sessions. Additionally, at site 1, the retest μ-map was coregistered to the test μ-map, and the PET attenuation-correction process was repeated for the test session based on the retest μ-map. Intersession repeatability was assessed via Bland-Altman plots, and within-subject coefficients of variation (wCVs) were calculated. Results: At site 1, 10 subjects with 11 measurable lesions were analyzed, and the wCVs for SUVmax and SUVpeak were 12.3% and 9.6%, respectively. At site 2, 11 subjects with 30 measurable lesions were analyzed, and the wCVs for SUVmax and SUVpeak were 9.5% and 8.8%, respectively. At site 1, repeating attenuation correction of the test PET data with the retest μ-map slightly improved repeatability, reducing the wCV to 10.1% for SUVmax and to 9.1% for SUVpeak For 8 of 11 lesions at site 1, the μ-map substitution altered the test-retest change by less than 5%, with no appreciable intersession μ-map differences or artifacts. Conclusion: The test-retest repeatability of SUVmax among hypermetabolic lesions on [18F]FDG PET/MRI, using data from 2 scanner models, was similar to the Quantitative Imaging Biomarker Alliance's wCV benchmark of 10%-12% for [18F]FDG PET/CT. Intersession μ-map variations had minimal negative impact on repeatability.

articles.title: B7H3-Targeted Molecular Imaging for Highly Specific Diagnosis and In Vivo Noninvasive Detection of B7H3 in Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: B7 homolog 3 (B7H3) is widely expressed in solid tumors, but its role in the diagnosis of breast cancer is unclear. We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH PET/CT in breast cancer patients. Methods: Thirty patients with diverse subtypes of breast cancer underwent both [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH and [18F]FDG PET/CT. Immunohistochemical staining for B7H3 was performed in 25 patients. Results: B7H3 positivity was detected in 84% of samples by immunohistochemistry. [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH demonstrated a higher lesion detection rate compared with [18F]FDG (96.8% vs. 92.4%) among 157 lesions. Median SUVmax was 9.5 in strongly positive lesions; bone metastases had the highest uptake (median SUVmax, 10.9). Imaging resulted in changing the stage or treatment in 8 patients. Hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative lesions showed the highest B7H3 positivity (87.5%) and uptake (median SUVmax, 10.5). Conclusion: [68Ga]Ga-B7H3-BCH PET/CT offers high sensitivity for staging advanced breast cancer and noninvasive B7H3 screening. It may influence clinical decisions and appears to reveal subtype-specific uptake, with a tendency to favor hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative disease.

articles.title: Brain-Specific Quantification of Somatostatin Receptor Expression: SUVmax and SUVRsss as Quantitative Correlates of the Krenning Score in Meningioma.
articles.abstract: Somatostatin receptor type 2 is highly expressed in meningiomas and can be quantified using [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET. The Krenning score, originally developed for [111In]In-octreotide scintigraphy, remains the standard visual grading system for somatostatin receptor expression and is widely used to guide eligibility for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. However, visual grading may not optimally translate to intracranial disease. This study evaluated the relationship between brain-specific quantitative PET parameters-SUVmax and SUV ratio normalized to the superior sagittal sinus (SUVRsss)-and the Krenning score in meningioma. Methods: This single-institution retrospective study included 44 patients (70 meningiomas) who underwent clinical vertex-to-thigh [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT. Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, SUVRsss, lesion size) were extracted from coregistered PET and MR images. Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess associations between imaging variables and Krenning score. Differences in quantitative PET parameters across Krenning categories were evaluated using Kruskal-Wallis test and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U test. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis using the Youden J index identified optimal cutoffs for clinically relevant thresholds (Krenning score of <3 vs. ≥3 and 3 vs. 4). Results: SUVRsss and SUVmax were strongly correlated with the Krenning score (SUVRsss: Spearman ρ = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82; SUVmax: Spearman ρ = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.85; P < 0.0001). PET parameters differed significantly across Krenning categories (all P < 0.001). SUVRsss optimal thresholds were 9.00 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.96) for Krenning scores of 2 versus 3 and 29.84 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.00) for Krenning scores of 3 versus 4. SUVmax optimal thresholds were 7.20 (AUC, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99) and 30.70 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.95-1.00), respectively. Conclusion: SUVRsss and SUVmax are complementary quantitative correlates of Krenning scores 2-4 in [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET-visible, MRI-measurable meningiomas. Brain-only PET evaluation may provide an alternative to liver- and spleen-based visual grading and reduce the need for whole-body imaging in selected settings. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve-derived SUV thresholds correspond to Krenning scores used for eligibility for treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, supporting further evaluation of quantitative PET parameters for theranostic decision-making for patients with meningioma.

articles.title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in Refractory Meningiomas: Results from the French Multicenter MELUTE Cohort.
articles.abstract: Evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas derives mainly from small, single-center studies. The French national multicenter MELUTE study aimed to consolidate these data using a standardized regimen within a compassionate-use program approved by a national multidisciplinary tumor board. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients with refractory meningiomas treated with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in 18 French centers between July 2022 and December 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of 7.4 GBq every 8 wk for up to 4 cycles. Clinical data (demographics, histologic World Health Organization grade [WHO], prior treatments, number of cycles, toxicity, progression, survival status as of October 1, 2025) were collected. Baseline [68Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were centrally reviewed. The primary endpoint was 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS) assessed using volumetric Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group criteria. Secondary endpoints were PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. Results: Sixty-nine patients were included (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 52% female): 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 without histology. Most had prior surgery (86%) or radiotherapy (93%); 32% received prior systemic therapy. Twelve patients (17%) did not complete 4 cycles; only one discontinuation was toxicity-related. Six-month PFS was 70% (95% CI, 58.7-80.4%). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3-18.5 mo), and median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached). Grade 3 adverse events, mainly lymphopenia, occurred in 16%. Meningioma WHO grade independently predicted PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use were protective; worse OS was associated with higher baseline tumor growth rate and prior systemic therapy. Conclusion: MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Design and Development of NeuroSphere PET: A Next-Generation 7-T MR-Compatible Dedicated Brain PET Scanner.
articles.abstract: PET is the most powerful imaging modality for studying neurotransmitters, receptors, and neuromodulation in humans, complementing the anatomic and hemodynamic information provided by MRI. However, PET temporal resolution remains constrained by sensitivity, limiting studies of fast, dynamic neurochemical processes. To address this gap, we are developing the Human Dynamic NeuroChemical Connectome, an imaging system integrating NeuroSphere PET, a novel ultra-high-sensitivity dedicated brain PET camera, with the Siemens Healthineers Magnetom Terra.X, a clinical 7-T MRI scanner. This article describes the design, engineering, and simulation-based performance estimation of NeuroSphere PET. Sensitivity maximization drove 2 core design choices: a partial spheric detector arrangement with a 32-cm inner diameter and 70% solid-angle coverage and the use of 26-mm lutetium oxyorthosilicate crystals for high stopping power (∼90% at 511 keV), coupled to silicon photomultipliers in a light-sharing, depth-of-interaction-capable configuration. The system comprises 872 detector blocks organized across 19 rings and 218 modules. At the detector level, measured performance includes energy resolution of approximately 11% full width at half maximum (FWHM), depth-of-interaction resolution of approximately 8 mm FWHM, and coincidence timing resolution of approximately 500 ps FWHM. System-level performance was evaluated using the ultrafast Monte Carlo PET simulator, accounting for realistic detector response, positron range, photon noncollinearity, and interdetector scatter. Sensitivity was estimated from a 30-cm uniform sphere, predicting a peak sensitivity of about 38% and a whole-brain average exceeding 25%. Spatial resolution and image quality were assessed through Derenzo phantom simulations evaluated at both the center of the field of view and 8 cm off-center, indicating that 1.6-mm structures can be resolved near the center of the field of view and that resolution of less than 2 mm can be maintained at the cortex. The system incorporates a 3-dimensional-printed MRI-compatible gantry, a dedicated 16-channel parallel transmit-receive radiofrequency head coil, and a custom radiofrequency shielding enclosure for simultaneous PET/MRI at 7 T. By targeting sensitivity an order of magnitude higher than that of commercial PET systems, NeuroSphere PET is expected to enable simultaneous neurochemical and hemodynamic studies with substantially improved spatiotemporal resolution, providing new insights into brain function and connectivity.

articles.title: Method of Detection: Why It's Important to Start Collecting this Parameter in Routine Practice.
Congratulations to the 2026 RSNA Outstanding Educator: Zehava Sadka Rosenberg, MD.
Latent Interpolation Learning Using Diffusion Models for Cardiac Volume Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging is a critical tool for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular disease, yet its utility is often limited by the sparse acquisition of 2D short-axis slices, resulting in incomplete volumetric information. Accurate 3D reconstruction from these sparse slices is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, but existing methods face challenges, including reliance on predefined interpolation schemes (e.g., linear or spherical), computational inefficiency, and dependence on additional semantic inputs such as segmentation labels or motion data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Cardiac Latent Interpolation Diffusion (CaLID) framework that introduces three key innovations. First, we present a data-driven interpolation scheme based on diffusion models, which can capture complex, non-linear relationships between sparse slices and improves reconstruction accuracy. Second, we design a computationally efficient method that operates in the latent space and speeds up generative 3D whole-heart upsampling time by a factor of 24, reducing computational overhead compared to previous methods. Third, with only sparse 2D CMR images as input, our method achieves SOTA performance against baseline methods, eliminating the need for auxiliary input such as morphological guidance, thus simplifying workflows. We further extend our method to 2D+T data, enabling the effective modeling of spatiotemporal dynamics and ensuring temporal coherence. Extensive volumetric evaluations and downstream segmentation tasks demonstrate that CaLID achieves superior reconstruction quality and efficiency. By addressing the fundamental limitations of existing approaches, our framework advances the state of the art for spatio and spatiotemporal whole-heart reconstruction, offering a robust and clinically practical solution for cardiovascular imaging. The code is available at https://github.com/niklasbubeck/calid.

articles.title: TSMCA-Net: A Multi-Granular Cross-Attention Framework for Cross-Session EEG-fNIRS Decoding.
articles.abstract: We propose TSMCA-Net, a lightweight cross-session EEG-fNIRS decoder that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with <1M parameters-70.6% fewer than the strongest baseline-while maintaining sub-8ms inference latency. TSMCA-Net decomposes multimodal interactions into three complementary views-temporal-spatial (TS), temporal-modal (TM), and spatial-modal (SM)-through structured multi-view factorization that separates heterogeneous dependency axes while preserving cross-branch information sharing. A Dynamic Multi-Scale Context module adaptively aggregates spatial dependencies on a unified scalp topology, while a causal lag modeling strategy captures delayed hemodynamic responses under strict temporal causality. An asymmetric cross-attention mechanism then integrates the multi-granular representations for role-aware fusion. Under a leave-one-session-out protocol on two public datasets, TSMCA-Net achieves the highest mean accuracy across three cognitive paradigms (71.41% MI, 86.36% MA, 80.30% WG), outperforming all 12 baselines in absolute accuracy and achieving statistical significance in 31 of 36 pairwise comparisons (p<0.05). Perturbation experiments demonstrate 38%-62% smaller accuracy degradation under simulated spatial perturbations.

articles.title: Low-dose vs standard-dose photon-counting CT for myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease: a prospective feasibility study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical utility of photon counting computed tomography (PCCT)-derived quantitative parameters for assessing interstitial lung disease (ILD) burden in patients with inflammatory idiopathic myopathy (IIM), comparing standard-dose (SD) and tin-filtered low-dose (LD) protocols, and to assess the added value of ultrathin reconstructions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single-centre prospective study (September 2023-November 2024), outpatients with IIM-ILD underwent two consecutive PCCT scans. Quantitative ILD features were extracted using a commercial deep-learning software (ContextFlow ADVANCE Chest CT). Primary analyses compared LD 1.0 mm with SD 1.0 mm reconstructions using Bland-Altman analysis, with exploratory analyses of ultrathin (0.4 mm) reconstructions. Correlation analyses between deep learning-derived quantitative parameters, visual assessment, and pulmonary function tests were performed. RESULTS: Forty-eight adults with IIM-ILD (40 females; mean age, 53.88 ± 11.13 years) were included. The LD protocol achieved a substantial dose reduction (CTDIvol: 0.77 vs 5.40 mGy) while maintaining good agreement with SD (mean net differences [MNDs] < 1% for all patterns). LD-1.0 mm protocol yielded higher volume of ground-glass opacity (MND, 0.98%) and lower volume of fibrosis extent (MND, -0.64%). Reticular pattern showed strong association with FVC% (rhoSD1.0mm = -0.62, p < 0.001) and DLCO% (rhoSD1.0mm = -0.73, p < 0.001), with similar correlations observed under LD acquisition (Δrho ≤ 0.02). Ultrathin reconstructions yielded greater measurement of bronchiectasis (MND, 0.13% on SD scans). CONCLUSION: LD PCCT serves as a radiation-sparing alternative for quantitative disease assessment. Ultrathin reconstructions provide limited additional value. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to validate the performance of LD PCCT for disease monitoring. KEY POINTS: Question Can LD photon-counting CT provide robust quantitative assessment of ILD burden in patients with inflammatory myopathy compared with SD imaging? Findings Deep learning segmentation yielded LD ILD patterns that closely matched SD results, with all MNDs below 1%. Clinical relevance LD PCCT maintains quantitative robustness and physiological validity for IIM-ILD assessment, with total disease burden showing good agreement with the SD protocol, offering a radiation-sparing alternative without compromising CT-physiology correlation.

articles.title: The role of cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement in patients with acute cardiac symptoms and troponin elevation in the era of high-sensitivity assays.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Diagnostic workup of patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no acute myocardial infarction (AMI) criteria is challenging. Cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) rules out obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Adding late iodine enhancement and extracellular volume fraction (CCTA + LIE/ECV) provides insights into myocardial injury. However, the impact on working diagnosis, agreement with discharge diagnosis, and mid-term safety of implementing CCTA + LIE/ECV in the emergency department remains uncertain. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective study on consecutive patients presenting, from June 2018 to February 2025, with acute chest pain or equivalents, elevated troponin, and no AMI diagnosis, excluding previously revascularized patients. Patients underwent CCTA to rule out obstructive CAD (≥ 50% stenosis). CCTA-negative patients underwent myocardial tissue characterization with LIE; if negative, ECV was quantified. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: modification of working diagnosis by CT. Secondary endpoints: agreement between CT and discharge diagnoses after standard-of-care assessment; mid-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in CT-negative patients. RESULTS: Among 191 patients (age 70 [55-79] years; 53% men), CCTA identified obstructive CAD in 76/191 (40%). LIE/ECV were positive in 58/106 (55%) of CCTA-negative cases, revealing myocarditis in 32/106 (30%), AMI with non-obstructive CAD in 8/106 (8%), Takotsubo in 14/106 (13%), amyloidosis in 3/106 (3%), and dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/106 (1%). CT modified the working diagnosis in 91/191 (48%) patients. Agreement between CT and discharge diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI 0.89-0.97). In patients with negative CCTA + LIE/ECV, no MACEs occurred after 24 [interquartile range, 19-29] months. CONCLUSION: In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative. KEY POINTS: Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.

articles.title: Impact of VI-RADS quality score on VI-RADS diagnostic performance for muscle invasion: the role of tumor size and reader experience.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the inter-reader agreement of the Vesical Imaging Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) quality scoring system and to assess its impact on the diagnostic performance for detecting muscle invasion. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 587 patients who underwent multiparametric bladder MRI before surgery. Three radiologists (two specialists and one non-genitourinary radiologist) independently assessed VI-RADS category and quality scores. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated using weighted kappa statistics. Associations between image quality, VI-RADS categorization, and tumor characteristics were analyzed using multivariable models. Diagnostic performance for muscle invasion was assessed at predefined VI-RADS thresholds and compared across quality groups and tumor size subgroups. RESULTS: A total of 7/587 (1.2%), 284/587 (48.4%), and 296/587 (50.4%) scans were VI-RADS quality score 0, 1, and 2, respectively. Inter-reader agreement for the final quality score was substantial (k = 0.628-0.702). Higher VI-RADS quality scores were associated with increased T2-weighted image VI-RADS scores (odds ratio [OR], 2.95; 95% confidence interval, 1.17-7.43; p = 0.021). In tumors < 3 cm, particularly for the less experienced reader, higher image quality was associated with increased positive predictive value (PPV) and accuracy at the VI-RADS ≥ 3 threshold (PPV: 51.0% vs 22.7%, p = 0.004; accuracy: 81.6% vs 71.7%, p = 0.023). No significant differences in diagnostic performance were observed across VI-RADS thresholds in tumors ≥ 3 cm. CONCLUSION: The VI-RADS quality scoring system demonstrated good inter-reader agreement. Optimal image quality improved diagnostic performance in small tumors and for the less experienced reader; however, because only one less experienced reader was included, this finding requires external validation. KEY POINTS: Question Does image quality, assessed by the VI-RADS quality score, influence diagnostic performance of VI-RADS for detecting muscle invasion in bladder cancer? Findings Higher image quality improved PPV and accuracy of VI-RADS, particularly in tumors < 3 cm and for the less experienced reader, while having limited impact in larger tumors. Clinical relevance Ensuring optimal MRI image quality enhances the reliability of VI-RADS interpretation, particularly in small tumors and non-specialized settings, and supports standardized imaging as a prerequisite for accurate bladder cancer staging.

articles.title: Alphabet Soup: Navigating the Grant Landscape and Why It Matters for Radiology Trainees.
Balloon-Occlusion Versus End-Hole Transarterial Chemoembolization for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of balloon-occluded transarterial chemoembolization (B-TACE) compared with conventional (cTACE) and drug-eluting-bead transarterial chemoembolization (DEB-TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched to 8 February 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing B-TACE with cTACE or DEB-TACE. Tumor response (mRECIST), overall survival, and adverse events were pooled using random-effects models; risk of bias was assessed with established tools. RESULTS: Nine studies (one randomized, eight observational; 1534 patients) were included. Complete response, objective response, disease control, and progressive disease did not differ significantly between groups, with moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity. Baseline tumors were larger in the balloon-occluded group (mean difference 4.34 mm; 95% CI 1.18- 7.50; p = 0.014). Exploratory study-level analyses suggested greater relative B-TACE effects with larger tumors, particularly for complete response and disease control.Overall survival favored B-TACE in the two studies with extractable hazard ratios (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.73; p = 0.002). Post-treatment liver enzymes, bilirubin, fever, and post-embolization syndrome did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in imaging response or safety were observed between intervention and comparator groups, while B-TACE was associated with a signal toward improved overall survival despite larger baseline tumors. Exploratory findings suggested that larger tumor size may be associated with a greater relative B-TACE effect. Given the limited evidence, these findings require confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: AI-enhanced routine CT for opportunistic osteoporosis screening and risk assessment.
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis-related fractures create a large and often preventable burden, yet many individuals undergoing CT for unrelated care do not receive skeletal assessment. This review evaluates artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled use of routine CT for opportunistic case-finding and risk assessment, with emphasis on the boundary between promising retrospective performance and safe clinical implementation. Automated vertebral segmentation and CT-derived bone-density estimation can reduce manual workload, and published diagnostic studies report high discrimination in selected cohorts. However, pooled estimates are heterogeneous because the reference standard, anatomical target, CT acquisition, reconstruction, contrast status, calibration method, prevalence, and validation design differ substantially across studies. These differences preclude a universal CT threshold or a universal minimum detector-row requirement; detector-row configuration should be considered together with the broader acquisition and reconstruction parameters. For implementation, AI should be deployed as a validated triage tool-not as a stand-alone diagnostic replacement for clinical assessment and indicated DXA/QCT. A credible pathway requires a defined CT-protocol eligibility check; pre-specified vertebral region of interest and exclusions; protocol- and contrast-aware quantification; scanner-specific quality assurance and calibration monitoring where applicable; external validation in representative populations; and an explicit route from an AI alert to confirmatory testing and treatment evaluation. AI may also enable concurrent vertebral-fracture and body-composition assessment, but clinical utility must be shown through downstream testing, treatment, fracture, workload, equity, and cost outcomes. The near-term priority is therefore not higher retrospective diagnostic performance alone, but reproducible, transparent, and prospectively evaluated integration into radiology workflows.

articles.title: Mammography and Ultrasonography for Symptomatic Male Breast Lesions: A PRISMA-DTA Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Male breast disease is uncommon, but symptomatic men require reliable differentiation between benign conditions and lesions warranting biopsy or oncologic management. This PRISMA-DTA (Preferred Reporting Items for a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies) systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy, clinical utility, and evidentiary limitations of mammography and ultrasonography for malignant versus benign male breast lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus were searched from inception to May 30, 2026. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO before journal submission (CRD420261429183). Eligible reports evaluated mammography or ultrasonography in male breast disease and provided extractable 2 × 2 diagnostic data. Methodological quality was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized separately for each modality using bivariate random-effects modeling and summary receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: Thirteen eligible reports were included. Seven mammography datasets and five ultrasonography datasets were available for quantitative synthesis. Mammography showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.840 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.705-0.921) and a specificity of 0.951 (95% CI, 0.884-0.980), whereas ultrasonography showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.881 (95% CI, 0.775-0.941) and a specificity of 0.958 (95% CI, 0.869-0.987). Although pooled specificity estimates were high, their magnitude may have been influenced by heterogeneous diagnostic thresholds, differential verification, variable follow-up, and sparse malignant case counts. Nine of 13 reports were judged to have an overall high risk of bias, and consistent paired head-to-head data were lacking. CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports mammography and ultrasonography as complementary tools in risk-stratified assessment of symptomatic male breast lesions. Pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence base is small and methodologically limited. Current data do not establish direct modality superiority, do not justify biopsy avoidance when clinical-imaging discordance persists, and do not determine the incremental value of routine combined imaging.

articles.title: Streamlining Collaborations to Overcome the Challenges Facing Theranostics Clinical Trials.
FDA Policy Changes on Stability Studies for PET Drugs Manufactured Within Networks.
Unverified Assumptions and Confounded Categories: A Closer Look at the Predicted Impact of MIPS Value Pathways on Diagnostic Radiology.
Clinical practice guidance for imaging selection in pulsatile tinnitus: an evidence-based expert consensus.
articles.abstract: Pulsatile tinnitus (PT) is a rhythmic sound synchronized with the patient's heartbeat that represents a complex diagnostic challenge with a broad spectrum of vascular and non-vascular etiologies. Persistent symptoms can severely impact mental health, yet a specific causative abnormality can be identified via targeted radiological imaging in more than 75% of cases. Improper imaging selection frequently leads to misdiagnosis, reduced therapeutic efficacy, and increased healthcare costs. The choice of imaging protocol must be guided by a thorough initial clinical evaluation, including detailed medical history, physical maneuvers, and otoscopic examinations. Commissioned by the Medical Imaging Center Branch of the Chinese Hospital Association, this evidence-based expert consensus guidance aims to provide structured recommendations for the strategic selection of imaging modalities in PT patients. The guidance explicitly distinguishes recommendations grounded in comparative diagnostic literature from those derived from formal expert consensus where high-level comparative evidence is limited.

articles.title: Direct probabilistic IMPT treatment planning with setup and range errors for neuro-oncological patients.
articles.abstract: Objective. To show computational feasibility of a previously proposed probabilistic planning approach on a neuro-oncological patient group, we compared probabilistic plans with (automated) robust plans for one patient (group A) that could achieve sufficient clinical target coverage and for four patients (group B) where target coverage had to be compromised due to organ-at-risk (OAR) dose constraints.Approach. The probabilistic approach is percentile-based and uses the fact that a (dose) percentile can be approximated as a linear combination of its expected value and standard deviation. This allows us to formulate objectives and constraints with patient-specific acceptance probabilities. The optimization has a nested structure: the inner optimization optimizes the beam weights for a given percentile estimate, while an outer loop iteratively updates and improves the accuracy of the percentile estimate. For every outer iteration, the optimization is warm-started from the previous iteration. Percentiles are efficiently calculated by sampling a polynomial chaos expansion of the dose-influence matrix.Main results. The patient in group A achieved cumulative OAR dose reductions (of OAR-related DVH-metrics) of 23.1 GyRBE, for identical target coverage. Target coverage improved for all patients in group B (the 10th percentile ofincreased up to 0.61 GyRBE), at the same time reaching cumulative OAR dose reductions (of OAR-related DVH-metrics) up to about 40 GyRBE. Probabilistic plans were optimized in 44 h to 226 h. For two representative patients, eliminating warm-starting (i.e. the outer loop) from the approach reduced total optimization times to below 10 h (which took originally 80 h and 141 h).Significance. Compared to robust optimization methods, the probabilistic approach achieves improved trade-offs between probabilistic target coverage and OAR sparing, potentially leading to better treatments.

articles.title: Integrating Histotripsy into Chemoimmunotherapy for Oligometastatic Recurrent Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: Case Report.
articles.abstract: The management of advanced, recurrent extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma has shifted toward prolonged systemic therapy including immune checkpoint inhibition. Incorporating local treatment for oligometastatic or oligoprogressive disease without interrupting systemic therapy remains challenging. Conventional liver-directed therapies frequently require a chemotherapy break. Histotripsy is a noninvasive, non-thermal, non-ionizing modality that permits continuation of systemic therapy. This case presents a 71-year-old woman with recurrent extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who developed multifocal hepatic metastases while receiving gemcitabine and durvalumab. She was deemed not a candidate for further radiation therapy or other locoregional therapies; thus, nine of ten hepatic lesions were treated with histotripsy in a single session. This case highlights the possibility of integrating histotripsy with chemoimmunotherapy by providing short-term local control of oligometastatic progression without the need to interrupt systemic treatment.Level of Evidence: Level 4, Case Report.

articles.title: Environmental impact of a radiology department: greenhouse gas emissions and primary energy accounting and strategies for sustainable practice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the environmental impact of a radiology department's operations (primary energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions (GHG); to identify the main levers for reduction. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data collection included measured and calculated energy consumption of imaging machines (2 MRI, 2 CT, 1 interventional radiology (IR) suite, 2 US, 3 radiography machines), workstations, lighting, ventilation; cooling and heating for imaging systems and rooms; materials/pharmaceuticals; external services (e.g. laundry and information technology (IT)). The electrical energy consumption of building systems, lighting, and IT equipment was primarily determined through measurements; other energy consumption figures were estimated using technical data and meteorological data. For the calculation of GHG emissions and primary energy consumption, a specialised tool using specific conversion factors from established environmental databases was developed. RESULTS: Our hospital switched from coal-based electricity to renewable electrical energy (hydropower), leading to a reduction in primary energy consumption (-64%) and GHG emissions (-92%) of the radiology department. Following this change, without a reduction in direct energy consumption, the MRI systems showed a marked reduction in primary energy consumption, although still having the highest primary energy consumption per exam (49.2 kWh compared to 13.9 kWh (CT1) and 48.9 kWh (IR)). After the transition to renewable energy, the major source of GHG emissions shifted from electrical energy toward materials/pharmaceuticals. CONCLUSION: Our findings support the transition to renewable energy sources for electricity, as a key strategy for reducing GHG emissions and primary energy demand of radiology departments. Following this shift, selecting materials and pharmaceuticals with lower emissions and primary energy factors can further mitigate the environmental impact. KEY POINTS: Question Radiology departments are significant sources of energy consumption and GHG emissions. Findings Adoption of renewable energy reduces primary energy consumption and GHG emissions. Critical relevance statement GHG emissions in a radiology department can be significantly reduced by transitioning to renewable energy sources. After this shift, emissions will mainly depend on the materials and pharmaceuticals used, such as disposable supplies and contrast agents.

articles.title: Multi-Institutional Review of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Use in Pediatric Patients.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Children at risk for pulmonary embolism (PE) may be treated with inferior vena cava (IVC) filter insertion when anticoagulation is impossible or ineffective. The purpose of this multi-institutional retrospective review is to better understand the indications and technical and clinical outcomes related to IVC filter placement and removal in pediatric patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was open to all institutions that placed IVC filters in pediatric patients. Data collected included demographics, indications, procedural details of filter insertion and/or removal, and clinical follow-up. Univariate analysis was performed. RESULTS: A total of 250 filters were placed in 242 pediatric patients (135 male) at 12 participating hospitals between October 1994 and June 2020. Thrombosis was present in 82.8% of patients, PE in 34.8%, and anticoagulation adverse events (AEs) or contraindications in 45.9%. Most filter insertions were technically successful (99.1%); 3.1% were associated with minor AEs, and 0.4% with moderate AEs. Breakthrough pulmonary embolism occurred in 1.4% following filter placement. Filter retrieval rate was 76%. Removal was technically successful in 88% of attempts and resulted in minor AEs in 1.1% and severe AEs in 6.5%. Minor, moderate, and severe device-associated AEs occurred in 8%, 1.6%, and 3.2% of filters, respectively. There was no correlation between age or weight and outcomes, including breakthrough PE, AEs, or mortality. CONCLUSION: IVC filter insertion in pediatric patients is feasible and associated with a high retrieval rate.

articles.title: Single-Session Ablative Radioembolization for Small Hepatocellular Carcinoma Is Associated with Lower Treatment-Episode Charges, Shorter Time to Treatment, and Reduced Travel Burden.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To test the hypothesis that, compared with conventional two-session transarterial radioembolization (TARE), single-session TARE (ssTARE) is associated with lower hospital charges, fewer modeled interventional radiology (IR) physician work relative value units (wRVUs), shorter consultation-to-treatment intervals, and less procedure-related travel in selected patients undergoing ablative TARE for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-institution retrospective review included 312 treatment episodes in 255 patients between January 2022 and April 2026, comprising 96 single-session ablative TARE episodes and 216 conventional TARE episodes. Conventional TARE was defined as mapping angiography with Tc-99m MAA administration, SPECT/CT, and lung shunt fraction calculation followed by Y-90 administration during a separate encounter. RESULTS: Ninety-three of 96 ssTARE attempts (96.9%) had successful Y-90 delivery. All treatments used glass microspheres. Mean recorded hospital charges were $118,656 for conventional TARE (n=202) and $86,193 for ssTARE (n=51), a 27.4% reduction (p < 0.001). Lower charges persisted in sensitivity analyses. ssTARE was associated with 17.9% fewer modeled IR physician wRVUs and 42.6% fewer modeled driving miles (p < 0.01). The primary consultation-to-treatment interval was 15 days shorter (p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: In selected patients with HCC, ssTARE was associated with lower recorded institutional charges, fewer modeled procedure-related travel miles, and a shorter consultation-to-treatment interval.

articles.title: Achieving detailed medial temporal lobe segmentation with upsampled isotropic training from implicit neural representation.
articles.abstract: Imaging biomarkers in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are important tools for diagnosing, tracking and treating Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurofibrillary tau pathology in AD is closely linked to neurodegeneration and generally follows a pattern of spread in the brain, with early stages involving subregions of the medial temporal lobe (MTL). Accurate segmentation of MTL subregions is needed to extract granular biomarkers of AD progression. MTL subregions are often imaged using T2-weighted (T2w) MRI scans that are highly anisotropic due to constraints of MRI physics and image acquisition, making it difficult to reliably model MTL subregions geometrically and extract morphological measures, such as thickness. In this study, we propose a segmentation framework for MTL subregions in isotropic space, in which an implicit neural representation is used to construct the isotropic training atlas from the anisotropic low-resolution T2w data, with T1w MRI as an auxiliary modality to support the INR and segmentation. In an independent test set, the morphological measures extracted using this isotropic model showed stronger effect sizes than those from models trained on anisotropic data in distinguishing participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from cognitively unimpaired individuals. In the test-retest analysis, the morphological measures extracted using the isotropic model showed greater stability than those from the anisotropic segmentation. This study demonstrates improved reliability of MRI-derived MTL subregion biomarkers without additional atlas annotation effort, which may more accurately quantify and track the relationship between AD pathology and brain atrophy for monitoring disease progression.

articles.title: Characterizing age-dependent diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility properties in 5xFAD Alzheimer's mouse brain using high-resolution MRI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating and progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. This study aimed to characterize magnetic susceptibility changes associated with beta-amyloid (Aβ) plaques during AD progression using diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measurements in the 5xFAD mouse model. METHODS: Ex vivo multi-echo gradient-echo imaging (MGRE) with a spatial resolution of 40 × 40 × 40 μm3 was performed in three age groups of 5xFAD mice (4, 12, and 18 months) using a 9.4T Bruker MRI scanner. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) was reconstructed, and DECOMPOSE-QSM was applied to derive diamagnetic component susceptibility (DCS) and paramagnetic component susceptibility (PCS). Aβ plaques were automatically detected based on DCS and quantified to assess age-dependent plaque accumulation, changes in plaque burden, and associated susceptibility alterations. Cortical regions were further segmented into plaque-detected and plaque-undetected regions to assess regional susceptibility variations among the three age groups. In addition, Aβ/ferritin immunostaining was performed on the imaged murine brains. RESULTS: The results demonstrated progressive, spatially heterogeneous, age-dependent accumulation of amyloid plaques, as evidenced by significant increases in plaque burden. In plaque-detected and whole-region cortical areas, DCS consistently shifted toward more negative values (greater diamagnetic susceptibility) with disease progression, while PCS became more positive (greater paramagnetic susceptibility). The concurrent increase in plaque burden, together with progressively more negative DCS and more positive PCS within plaques, is consistent with increasing diamagnetic and paramagnetic tissue contributions associated with amyloid and iron-related pathology, respectively. Histological analysis showed colocalized Aβ aggregation and ferritin deposition within plaques, both of which increased with age. CONCLUSIONS: The decomposed susceptibility components, DCS and PCS, provide complementary biophysical information beyond conventional QSM, enabling improved characterization of plaque-associated susceptibility changes during AD progression. High-resolution MRI facilitates the visualization and detection of individual plaques, allowing detailed analysis of their susceptibility properties. These findings highlight the importance of high-resolution MRI and the potential of diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measures as sensitive imaging biomarkers for monitoring neurodegenerative pathology.

articles.title: Patient selection for proton therapy in lung cancer: Updating and internal-external cross-validation of a normal tissue complication probability model for acute oesophageal toxicity.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To externally validate and update a published normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model for the prediction of Grade ≥ 2 acute oesophageal toxicity (AOT) in lung cancer patients receiving (chemo-)radiotherapy (predictors: concurrent chemotherapy, gender, tumour stage, mean oesophagus dose (MOD)). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patient cohorts from four centres were available. Initial external validation was performed by assessing model performance. Heterogeneity of performance across cohorts was evaluated using an internal-external cross validation (IECV) method. Based on the IECV procedure, parameters were added or removed from the model to lower heterogeneity in model performance across cohorts with the aim to create a model that performed uniformly well across centres. Ridge regression was used to create the final model and bootstrapping techniques were applied to perform further internal validation. RESULTS: Out of 937 patients, 444 (47%) had Grade ≥ 2 AOT. External validation indicated model recalibration was necessary for 1 cohort and model revision for another. IECV showed heterogeneity of performance of the original model across cohorts. To lower heterogeneity in model performance, the predictors concurrent chemotherapy, gender, and tumour stage were removed from the model, and overall treatment time (OTT) was added. The final model containing MOD and OTT as predictors showed low levels of heterogeneity in model performance (I2 of 0% for all performance measures) with optimism-corrected AUC of 0.75, calibration intercept of -0.01 and slope of 1.26. CONCLUSION: The validation and updating of an NTCP-model for AOT resulted in a prediction model performing well in varying patient cohorts. Therefore, this updated model was added to the national indication protocol to select lung cancer patients for proton radiotherapy.
authors: national platform for proton therapy for lung cancer

articles.title: Postnatal Dynamics of Choroid Plexus Cysts in Newborns and Infants: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Purpose Choroid plexus cysts (CPC) are frequently detected prenatally and are generally considered benign. However, data on their postnatal course, growth dynamics, and clinical relevance are limited. This study investigates the long-term development, growth patterns, and resolution of CPC in newborns and infants. Materials and Methods We retrospectively analysed 251 CPC in 164 patients admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit between 2014 and 2024. CPC were assessed using serial cranial ultrasonography. Growth dynamics were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and chi-square testing. Results CPC were identified in both preterm and term infants, with a mean CPC size of 4.1 mm at diagnosis. Of 177 CPC with serial imaging data, 40% were not present on initial scans and appeared postnatally. The median time to resolution was 108 days. Many CPC initially increased in size before decreasing or resolving completely. A chi-square analysis showed a significant shift in growth behaviour between the 6- and 12-week follow-up groups (p = 0.006). No infant required intervention related to CPC. Conclusion Postnatal CPC often follow a benign, self-limiting course, meaning they tend to resolve naturally over time, with dynamic growth patterns. Routine monitoring of isolated CPC in asymptomatic infants may not be needed in all cases. Ziel Choroidplexuszysten (CPC) werden häufig pränatal festgestellt und gelten im Allgemeinen als gutartig. Allerdings liegen nur begrenzte Daten zu ihrem postnatalen Verlauf, ihrer Wachstumsdynamik und ihrer klinischen Relevanz vor. Diese Studie untersucht die langfristige Entwicklung, die Wachstumsmuster und die Rückbildung von CPC bei Neugeborenen und Säuglingen. Materialien und Methoden Wir analysierten retrospektiv 251 CPC bei 164 Patienten, die zwischen 2014 und 2024 auf eine neonatologische Intensivstation aufgenommen wurden. Die CPC wurden mittels serieller kranialer Sonographie beurteilt. Die Wachstumsdynamik wurde mittels Kaplan-Meier-Überlebensanalyse und Chi-Quadrat-Test ausgewertet. Ergebnisse CPC wurden sowohl bei Frühgeborenen als auch bei termingeborenen Säuglingen festgestellt, wobei die durchschnittliche CPC-Größe bei der Diagnose 4,1 mm betrug. Von 177 CPC mit seriellen Bildgebungsdaten waren 40 % bei den ersten Untersuchungen nicht nachweisbar und traten postnatal auf. Die mediane Zeit bis zur Rückbildung betrug 108 Tage. Viele CPC nahmen zunächst an Größe zu, bevor sie sich verkleinerten oder vollständig zurückbildeten. Eine Chi-Quadrat-Analyse zeigte eine signifikante Verschiebung im Wachstumsverhalten zwischen den 6- und 12-Wochen-Nachbeobachtungsgruppen (p = 0,006). Bei keinem Säugling war eine interventionelle Behandlung im Zusammenhang mit dem CPC erforderlich. Schlussfolgerung Postnatale CPC zeigen in der Regel einen gutartigen und selbstlimitierenden Verlauf mit dynamischen Wachstumsmustern und spontaner Rückbildung. Eine routinemäßige Verlaufskontrolle isolierter CPC bei asymptomatischen Säuglingen ist möglicherweise nicht in allen Fällen erforderlich.

articles.title: Automated segmentation-based emergency CT radiomics for predicting functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia in primary brainstem hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary brainstem hemorrhage (PBSH) is associated with high mortality, disability, and uncertain early outcomes. Emergency non-contrast CT (NCCT) is the earliest imaging examination, but conventional assessment may not fully capture hematoma heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop an automated segmentation-based emergency NCCT radiomics framework for predicting poor functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia (PSP) in PBSH. METHODS: This retrospective study included 372 patients with PBSH, comprising a training set (n = 182), an internal test set (n = 79), and a temporal internal validation set (n = 111). Hematomas were segmented using a three-dimensional U-Net. Manual and automated segmentation-based radiomics models were compared, and automated segmentation-derived radiomics features were integrated with conventional radiological predictors to construct combined models for poor functional outcome and PSP. RESULTS: The automated segmentation-based radiomics model showed comparable performance to the manual segmentation-based model across all three datasets. The combined prognostic model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.923, and 0.858 in the training, internal test, and temporal internal validation sets, with higher AUCs and lower Brier scores than the conventional radiological model. The combined PSP model (AUCs: 0.828, 0.742, 0.681) showed no consistent improvement. SHAP identified hematoma classification as the most influential prognostic predictor. CONCLUSIONS: Automated segmentation-based NCCT radiomics is feasible for early risk stratification in PBSH. The combined prognostic model showed good discrimination and potential complementary value beyond conventional CT assessment. The PSP model remains exploratory and requires further refinement and validation.

articles.title: Sonographic findings in fontan-associated liver disease across pediatric and adult patients: A cross-sectional imaging study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to characterize sonographic hepatic findings across pediatric, adolescent, and adult Fontan patients and to examine their cross-sectional relationships with time since Fontan completion and chronological age. As a secondary objective, we explored a composite score integrating complementary sonographic findings. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a prospectively established single-center Fontan cohort, hepatic ultrasound findings from 153 patients were evaluated, including gray-scale imaging, Doppler assessment, and shear-wave elastography performed according to institutional acquisition protocols. Individual sonographic findings were analyzed as the primary imaging outcomes. Cross-sectional associations with time since Fontan completion were assessed using sex-adjusted regression models; additional models simultaneously included chronological age, time since Fontan completion, and sex to examine their closely related contributions. A secondary exploratory 5-point composite score integrating five complementary sonographic domains was evaluated descriptively. RESULTS: Longer time since Fontan completion was associated cross-sectionally with greater IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, structural abnormality, and hepatic nodularity in sex-adjusted analyses. Chronological age and time since Fontan completion were nearly collinear (r = 0.970). When both variables and sex were included simultaneously, associations with IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, and structural classification were attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas hepatic nodularity remained associated with time since Fontan completion (OR = 1.22/year; 95% CI 1.03-1.45; p = 0.024). Complete composite-score data were available in 101 patients; mean scores were 0.81 ± 0.88, 2.15 ± 1.26, 3.18 ± 0.80, and 4.27 ± 0.80 across < 5-, 5-<10-, 10-<20-, and ≥ 20-year post-Fontan categories, respectively. In 15 patients with serial examinations, scores were higher at the later examination in 10 and unchanged in five (p = 0.004). In a stratified subset of 40 independently reread examinations, interobserver agreement was high for liver size (ICC = 0.922) and IVC diameter (ICC = 0.947), whereas agreement for qualitative sonographic findings was lower (κ = 0.202-0.369). CONCLUSION: Sonographic vascular, morphologic, structural, elastographic, and nodular abnormalities differed across patients examined at increasing intervals after Fontan completion. However, because chronological age and Fontan duration were nearly collinear, this cross-sectional study cannot determine whether these imaging gradients reflect duration of Fontan physiology, chronological maturation, or both. Hepatic nodularity showed the most robust association with time since Fontan completion in simultaneous models. The composite score provides a secondary exploratory framework for integrating complementary sonographic findings but requires prospective longitudinal and external validation. The limited interobserver agreement for qualitative findings further emphasizes the need for standardized image interpretation and supports the exploratory status of the composite score.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS for identifying pathological complete response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether post-chemoradiotherapy neoadjuvant chemotherapy Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (nacVI-RADS) is associated with pathological complete response (pCR), and to assess its diagnostic performance and inter-reader agreement in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 73 patients with non-metastatic cT2-4aN0-2 M0 bladder cancer who underwent cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy followed by radical or partial cystectomy between 2009 and 2024. Two radiologists independently assigned post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS scores on MRI. For the primary diagnostic analysis, scores were dichotomized as < 3 and ≥ 3. The reference standard was bladder pCR, defined as ypT0 on pathological assessment. RESULTS: pCR was achieved in 46 of 73 patients (63%). The pCR rate was higher among patients with nacVI-RADS < 3 than among those with nacVI-RADS ≥ 3 for both readers (reader 1: 77% vs. 39%, p = 0.002; reader 2: 74% vs. 39%, p = 0.008). The sensitivity and specificity of nacVI-RADS < 3 for identifying pCR were 78% and 59% for reader 1 and 80% and 52% for reader 2, respectively. Inter-reader agreement was excellent (κ = 0.845; 95% CI, 0.687-0.962). CONCLUSION: Post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS < 3 was associated with pCR and showed moderate diagnostic performance with excellent inter-reader agreement in patients with MIBC. Post-chemoradiotherapy nacVI-RADS may provide useful complementary information for response assessment. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Burnout and psychosocial working conditions in a multidisciplinary hospital radiology team: a cross-sectional study using the job demands-resources framework.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Burnout is a major concern in hospital radiology, but data on psychosocial work conditions remain limited. Using the job demands-resources (JD-R) framework, this study examined burnout and its associations with psychosocial work factors across professional groups in a German university hospital radiology department. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted among radiologists and non-physician staff. Burnout was measured using the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI); psychosocial work conditions were assessed with COPSOQ III. Descriptive analyses, correlations, and hierarchical linear regressions were performed to evaluate associations between job demands, job resources, and burnout dimensions (personal, work-related, and patient-related burnout). RESULTS: Sixty-three participants (≤ 28 to ≥ 61 years; 37 women) were included. Personal and work-related burnout exceeded patient-related burnout. Non-physician staff reported higher personal burnout than radiologists. Job demands strongly correlated with personal (r = 0.686) and work-related burnout (r = 0.748), whereas associations with resources were weaker. In regression analyses, job demands were strongly associated with personal (R² = 0.62) and work-related burnout (R² = 0.60), without significant incremental resource effects. For patient-related burnout, job resources demonstrated an independent inverse association (total R² = 0.30). Higher burnout was associated with lower job satisfaction and greater sickness absence. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory single-centre study, burnout in hospital radiology was primarily associated with psychosocial job demands, particularly work-life conflict, workload, and role conflicts, whereas job resources showed weaker associations except for patient-related burnout. These findings suggest a predominantly demand-driven pattern within the JD-R framework and indicate that psychosocial working conditions may represent targets for intervention. KEY POINTS: Question Which psychosocial job demands and resources show the strongest associations with burnout among radiology staff in a university hospital department? Findings Work-life conflict, quantitative demands, and role conflicts showed the strongest associations with personal and work-related burnout among radiology staff. Critical relevance statement Burnout in hospital radiology was predominantly associated with organisational stressors, highlighting the relevance of psychosocial working conditions for organisational monitoring and intervention planning.

articles.title: The added value of post-mortem MRI in forensic imaging: an observational study in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In the Netherlands, post-mortem radiology aids forensic investigation, using a full-body post-mortem computed tomography (PMCT) scan and a post-mortem magnetic resonance imaging (PMMRI) scan in specific cases. Application of PMMRI varies between countries and institutions in the absence of international guidelines. This study analyses current use and added value of PMMRI in a single forensic imaging institution in the Netherlands. MATERIALS AND METHODS: All post-mortem cases scanned between July 2024 and July 2025 were included, except non-accidental injury protocol cases. The (contra-)indications for additional PMMRI scans in addition to PMCT were recorded. On the same day as image evaluation, added value was scored by the forensic radiologist and consultant using the following options: additional finding, exclusion of a finding, confirmation of PMCT and no added value. RESULTS: PMMRI was conducted in 47.4% of all cases, indicated by suspected strangulation, penetrating injuries, blunt force trauma and lesions seen on PMCT. In suspected strangulation, PMMRI neck showed additional findings or exclusion of findings in 31/46 cases, while PMMRI brain had the lowest added value in 13/25 cases. PMMRI thorax and abdomen showed additional findings in 14/20 and 4/9 cases of penetrating trauma, respectively. Additional findings were found in 10/15 PMMRI brain scans and 6/8 PMMRI thorax scans, based on PMCT. CONCLUSION: Application of PMMRI in addition to PMCT is currently used in a targeted manner. In cases of strangulation and penetrating injuries, additional or excluded findings were found. Therefore, adding PMMRI in these specific cases can be of added value. KEY POINTS: Question What is the added value of post-mortem MRI in forensic cases, in the absence of international guidelines and standardised indications? Findings Additional findings were observed in post-mortem MRI examinations indicated for soft tissue injuries caused by penetrating force and in cases of suspected strangulation. Critical Relevance Statement The criminal investigation can be optimised by using post-mortem MRI in addition to post-mortem CT, either by showing additional findings on post-mortem MRI not seen on CT, or by excluding findings with higher certainty.

articles.title: CT-fluoroscopy-guided lumbar epidural steroid injections: trainee participation, radiation dose, and procedural time.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Compare patient radiation, procedure time, and immediate post-procedural pain relief for CT-fluoroscopy (CTF)-guided lumbar epidural steroid injections (ESIs) performed by attendings alone versus with trainee participation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-institution study analyzed 371 consecutive CTF-guided lumbar ESIs (2018-2025) performed by attendings (n = 93) or by trainees under direct attending supervision (n = 278). Patient and procedural characteristics and outcomes were compared using Welch t-tests and chi-squared tests. Total dose length product (DLP) was separated into planning-scan and procedural components. Linear mixed-effects models were adjusted for age, sex, injection approach, planning CT omission, and academic year, with a random intercept for supervising attending. RESULTS: Total DLP was higher for trainee injections (53.7 ± 52.0 vs 31.7 ± 40.6 mGy∙cm, p < 0.001), driven by the planning CT (37.7 ± 47.3 vs 16.4 ± 32.2 p < 0.001); procedural DLP was similar (15.6 ± 10.3 vs 15.3 ± 11.9 mGy∙cm, p = 0.83). After adjustment, trainee participation was not associated with total or procedural DLP (geometric mean ratio 0.99 for both; 95% CIs 0.81-1.21 and 0.84-1.17). Proceduralist group explained 7% of total DLP variance; planning CT omission and supervising attending added 38% and 10%, respectively. Planning CT omission, practiced by two of seven attendings, declined from 53% of procedures in 2019-2020 to none after 2022. Trainee procedures took longer (20.0 ± 6.3 vs 18.3 ± 4.2, p = 0.005). Immediate pain reduction was similar (3.5 ± 2.9 vs 3.4 ± 2.6 points, p = 0.81). CONCLUSION: Trainee participation in CTF-guided lumbar ESIs was associated with modestly longer procedures but not increased procedural radiation. Higher total radiation with trainees reflected increasing use of planning CT and attending practice variation rather than trainee performance.

articles.title: IgG4-related disease of the pelvic floor musculature mimicking neoplasm: a case report with imaging-pathologic correlation.
articles.abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition that can form tumefactive mass-like lesions and mimic malignancy across organ systems. We describe a rare presentation involving the deep pelvic floor musculature with imaging-pathologic correlation while underscoring diagnostic pitfalls. A 49-year-old man with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, night sweats, and left lower quadrant abdominal pain underwent CT of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated a right posterior pelvic sidewall mass and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Pelvic MRI demonstrated an ill-defined intramuscular mass centered in the right iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus muscles. Relative to skeletal muscle, the lesion demonstrated iso- to low T1 signal intensity, intermediate T2 signal intensity, restricted diffusion, and moderate, diffuse contrast enhancement, raising concern for neoplasm or an inflammatory process. Image-guided biopsy revealed fibrotic soft tissue with severe lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and increased IgG4-reactive plasma cells. The IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio was > 75%, consistent with IgG4-RD when integrated with the clinical, laboratory, imaging and pathologic findings. IgG4-related disease with mass-like involvement of the pelvic floor musculature has not, to the best of our knowledge, been previously reported in the English literature. This entity can present as an ill-defined, enhancing, diffusion-restricting intramuscular mass and therefore may mimic a neoplastic process.

articles.title: Test order, timing, and multidisciplinary review predict management change in sequential fluoroscopic and MR defecography.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether sequential fluoroscopic defecography (FLD) and MR defecography (MRD) change clinical management of patients with pelvic floor dysfunction and to identify factors associated with management change. METHODS: Multi-institutional retrospective study including adults who underwent both FL and MR defecography within 3 years, without interval surgery. Primary outcome was management change attributed to the second examination. Clinical information, test order & timing, multidisciplinary review, and imaging variables were compared between patients with and without management change. Univariate analyses were performed overall and by first-modality subgroup. Multivariable logistic regression was performed in the overall cohort. RESULTS: Of 46 patients, 24 underwent FLD first and 22 underwent MRD first. Management changed after second examination in 23.9% (11/46). FLD-first order (adjusted OR, 72.70; 95% CI, 2.77-1909.81; p = 0.010), shorter interval between examinations (adjusted OR per 30 days, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-1.00; p = 0.038), and wider MR resting anorectal angle (adjusted OR per degree, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.02-1.20; p = 0.016) were independent predictors of management change. MRD after FLD showed more frequent new second-test abnormalities than FLD after MRD (16/24 [66.7%] vs. 5/22 [22.7%], p = 0.0037), particularly new cystocele detection (41.7% vs. 0%, p = 0.0006).
